relations.statement: A vertex gauge neutralizing all edges exists iff transport along every closed walk based at the root is trivial
relations.hypotheses: finite graph, root vertex, group-valued edge labelling

lemmas.statement: The finite dressing identity (dress_eq_one_iff and neutralizable_iff_closed_walks) is a statement about finite graphs and group elements only. It contains no continuous time parameter, no one-parameter unitary group and no Hamiltonian constraint, so it does not imply emergent time evolution or a Wheeler-DeWitt reading.
lemmas.lean_skeleton: -- scope statement, not a formal theorem; no Lean claim made

near_misses.claim: A finite clock of period N yields a one-parameter unitary group, i.e. continuous time with a Stone generator.
near_misses.rejecting_invariant: A finite clock gives only a cyclic group Z_N of discrete steps; a continuous one-parameter group is not supplied.

near_misses.claim: A pure-gauge dressing (trivial holonomy) is a Wheeler-DeWitt Hamiltonian constraint solution.
near_misses.rejecting_invariant: Trivial holonomy is a finite group-theoretic condition; there is no gravitational Hamiltonian or reparameterization-invariant dynamics in it.

open_obligations: No host-verified source for the relational-time or Wheeler-DeWitt reading; the target remains open and imported.
The clock-dressed history generator and its intertwining identity are not in KNOWN+, so they are not cited.
Continuous time, Stone generator and gravitational Hamiltonian constraint are assumptions, not derived.
